selector.why: The presence of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, onychodystrophy, and multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa, along with numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, specifically support Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome.
